Collects, manages, and analyzes large physiological datasets from laboratory, field, and wearable sensor studies.
Coordinates and leads field research teams conducting studies at military installations.
Develops technical reports, scientific manuscripts, presentations, and research documentation.
Collaborates with investigators and research teams to translate physiological data into actionable findings and recommendations.

Qualifications

Proficiency with R, SPSS, and/or MATLAB; experience with SAS and Excel is also relevant to the PWS tasks.
Ability to coordinate and lead teams executing field studies at military installations.
Strong scientific analysis, manuscript preparation, technical writing, and presentation capabilities.

Ability to communicate (both in written and oral settings) to larger audiences.

Ph.D. in Environmental Physiology.
Subject matter expertise in physiological responses to heat, cold, and high terrestrial altitude.
Experience designing and developing research protocols involving environmental extremes.

Role Title: Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant

Start Date: September 2027

Location: Leeds, Manchester or Edinburgh

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Launch your career on projects that help transform brownfield land, protect communities and support a more sustainable future. At Tetra Tech, you’ll work alongside experienced specialists, develop practical consultancy skills and contribute to projects that form part of our ambition to improve the lives of 1 billion people.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant, you will join our Geo team, delivering geo-environmental consultancy services supported by in-house ground investigation expertise. You will work across contaminated land, site investigation, brownfield redevelopment and geotechnical engineering projects for clients in sectors including property and regeneration, defence estates and transport.

Your Impact in this position

You will support the design, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental ground investigations. Your work will include desk studies, accurate collection and interpretation of site data, ground gas and groundwater monitoring, assessment of findings and production of detailed technical reports. This is an excellent opportunity to gain varied project experience and build a long-term career within a growing team.

5 Core Capabilities

Ground investigation: Support the planning, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental investigations across a range of sites and sectors.
Geo-environmental assessment: Undertake desk-based studies and develop your understanding of contaminated land, brownfield redevelopment, site investigation and geotechnical engineering.
Site data and monitoring: Collect, analyse and interpret site information accurately, including ground gas and groundwater monitoring data.
Technical reporting: Produce clear, detailed and well-structured reports that communicate findings and support sound project decisions.
Professional development and collaboration: Work effectively both independently and as part of a team, use initiative, build strong communication skills and work towards professional qualification with support from mentors and colleagues.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

You will have, or expect to achieve, at least a 2:1 degree in geology, engineering geology, environmental science or a related subject. Enthusiasm, analytical ability, strong written, communication and presentation skills, and a commitment to professional development are essential. Relevant work experience, such as a placement, is desirable. A full driving licence is required. Some projects may require security clearance, so you must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate clearance.

Working Environment

Based in either Leeds, Manchester or Edinburgh you will work across office, project and site environments, with travel required to client and investigation sites. Hybrid working is available; however, as this is a graduate role, you will be expected to spend more time in the office initially to support training, mentoring and your transition into the team. As your knowledge, confidence and competence develop, greater flexibility may be available in line with project and team requirements.

new_jobs.description:
Join Tetra Tech and apply your geospatial survey expertise to projects that shape infrastructure, water and environmental outcomes. Work with advanced LiDAR, UAV, GNSS and photogrammetry toolsets, lead high‑performing teams and deliver technically rigorous surveys that make a measurable difference.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

You will lead planning and delivery of complex geospatial survey programmes (topographic, control, boundary, measured building, volumetric) across multidisciplinary projects. The role combines hands‑on field leadership with responsibility for survey methodology, equipment maintenance (GNSS/GPS, total stations, terrestrial/mobile LiDAR, UAV platforms), data processing and production of CAD/3D/point‑cloud deliverables. You will prepare method statements, risk assessments and ensure compliance with standards and client specifications.

Your Impact in this position

As Principal/Senior Geospatial Surveyor you will mentor and develop junior surveyors, set QA/QC standards for field acquisition and processing, and act as the technical lead on client engagement and bid inputs. Your work will improve design accuracy, reduce project risk and support better asset management decisions for clients across infrastructure, energy and environmental sectors.

Core Capabilities

Leadership & Team Development — Lead, allocate and coach site teams; foster technical growth and safe working practices to raise delivery standards.
Field Survey Planning & Execution — Design and supervise complex field campaigns using GNSS, total station, laser scanning and UAV photogrammetry/LiDAR with robust QA/QC.
Geospatial Data Processing & Modelling — Process, register and classify point clouds, perform georeferencing, feature extraction and accuracy assessment to produce CAD, BIM and point‑cloud outputs.
Equipment & Systems Competence — Operate and maintain GNSS/GPS, total stations, terrestrial LiDAR and drone platforms; optimise workflows and troubleshoot on site.
Client Engagement & Compliance — Define survey scope with clients, prepare technical bid material, method statements and reports while ensuring regulatory and specification compliance.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

Degree or HND in Surveying/Geomatics/Geospatial Science or equivalent experience. Proven experience with GNSS, total station and LiDAR; competent in Leica Reg360/Cyclone, Leica Infinity, AutoCAD, ReCap or equivalents. Strong leadership, client‑facing skills and commitment to site safety. Driving licence and willingness to travel. Professional membership (RICS/CICES), UAV operations and Revit modelling desirable.

Position Overview

This position will assist the project team on civil/ environmental engineering design, investigation/ remediation , and other projects.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in civil or environmental engineering.
Typically requires 0-2 years of experience.
Engineer-in-Training (EIT) preferred.
Proficiency in AutoCAD. Civil 3D experience a plus.
Drainage design experience is a plus.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Preliminary data evaluation and analytical skills.
Ability to assist in the preparation of the major components of routine deliverables (i.e., tables, figures, appendices, etc.).
Exhibits strong work ethic, positive attitude, and general enthusiasm for the work.
Ability to safely perform various routine field activities including but not limited to applying proper sampling techniques for all environmental media and overseeing and directing subcontractors.

Essential Duties

Engineering design activities:
Assist project team in the development of engineering documents including plans, calculations, specifications and reports.
Use of AutoCAD/AutoCAD 3D to support design projects.
Provide quality assurance during construction.
Prepare technical reports by coordinating figures, data tables, site descriptions, and other necessary details to ensure report completeness.

Field activities:
Assists other technical staff in calibration of sampling/monitoring equipment, soil sampling, well installation, development and purging, groundwater sampling, vapor/indoor air sampling, remediation monitoring, and oversight.

Physical Demands/Work Environment Conditions

This position requires work in the field as well as in the office. Fieldwork includes working independently or as part of a larger team at exterior project sites (i.e., industrial/brownfield facilities, monitoring wells, treatment systems, construction projects) to perform sample collection, recording of operational/meter parameters, and oversight of subcontractors (e.g., drillers, heavy equipment operators, truckers). These field activities require the ability to drive to different project sites and physically move around outdoors in various terrains, in adverse weather conditions and occasionally for extended or irregular hours. Conducting work involves the use of hand-held monitoring instruments and tools, as well as water sampling equipment, which requires the ability to routinely lift and carry objects, stand, walk, reach, bend, squat, kneel and twist. Office work is primarily stationary/sedentary using a computer and keyboard/mouse requiring repetitive hand movements.

is seeking a Technical Partner

new_jobs.title: Environmental Designer with Energy Analysis Specialty, San Francisco
new_jobs.description:
Who is Atelier Ten?

Thank you for asking! Kindness and curiosity are some of Atelier Ten’s core tenets.

We are a team of environmental designers and carbon strategists championing for a healthier planet by leveraging our vast, collective knowledge of sustainable spaces. We help bring beauty and efficiency to every building, because like Maybelline, not all buildings are “born with it.” We work with architects, engineers, owners, and other stakeholders to accomplish their sustainability, wellness, functionality, and visual goals. We don’t just follow the trends of the industry, we trailblaze new paths to create high performance, sustainable, and award-winning buildings. Atelier Ten is a member company of Surbana Jurong (“SJ”), a global urban, infrastructure and managed services consulting firm based in more than 120 offices across 40 countries.

What is this role on a high level?

Let’s take a moment to see the overview of the role before we get into the nitty gritty.

We want you to be Atelier Ten San Francisco’s newest full-time Environmental Designer with a specialty in Energy Analysis with the goal of collaborating on projects to achieve energy efficiency and carbon emissions reduction goals. You would help produce technical deliverables, perform whole building energy modeling, develop engineering strategies for building systems (HVAC), consult on projects, and lead the industry in decarbonizing the built environment. You would be an integral member of an interdisciplinary environmental design consulting group and a key member of the company’s Energy Analysis practice.

What Your Day-to-day Looks Like

Days at Atelier Ten are filled with a large variety of project types from offices, labs to large masterplans. We promise to keep you challenged and never bored. Here are some regular tasks you may encounter:

Learn our internal methodologies that follow the energy analysis protocols of ASHRAE 90.1 (and other industry, state, or local standards) for new and existing building projects in any location or climate zone. Participate in our customized training program to build on your already robust critical thinking skills, root your knowledge based on first principals of buildings science and deliver analyses for world-class projects and clients.
Develop shoe-box and whole building energy models (in IES-VE and/or eQuest) to support a range of energy analyses for building design. Evaluate envelope performance, massing, and mechanical system optioneering across diverse climate zones and standards.
Identify and analyze net-zero energy and carbon strategies based on various metrics (i.e. carbon emissions, time of use rates, source/site, etc.)
Support senior staff to coordinate sustainability assessments, energy and thermal comfort analysis, energy benchmarking, development of climate impact mitigation strategies, life cycle cost analysis etc. on building and planning projects.
Collaborate with Atelier Ten’s integrated design groups to support the full range of our services, which include environmental design consulting, daylight and façade analysis, and benchmarking.
Use both analytical and computational methods to analyze unique and complex building physics and building systems.
Assist colleagues with energy analysis-related work which includes simulating buildings to arrive at carbon emissions calculations, annual cost analysis and life cycle cost analysis.
Review and interpret project architectural and mechanical design documentation for the purposes of performing whole building energy model simulations.
Cross-disciplinary collaboration with architects, MEP engineers, design team members, and internal environmental design teams to make energy and carbon emissions improvement recommendations.
Work with Atelier Ten’s Energy Analysis practice to develop new approaches and tools to improve team efficiency.
Prepare written summaries of work and technical reports for clients or other stakeholders.
Develop and maintain in-house databases and spreadsheet tools, methods and standards.
Attend site visits, project meetings and present analyses to the stakeholders.

What We Are Looking For

Hopefully you’re on board so far and excited about what your days at Atelier Ten will look like. We do have a few items on our wish list for you to become the next great Atelier Tenner. We are looking for someone who is curious, proactive, self-motivated with an appreciation and willingness to learn on multiple projects. They should have attention to detail, a desire to problem-solve, grit, and an open mind to learn from colleagues, clients and the training resources available. They will possess an eye for improving existing processes, interest in tool building, and communicating ideas and complex technical concepts to any audience. They will thrive when working in a collaborative environment and understand that an energy analyst’s work is part of the integrative design process; they will embrace the nature of iterative design and be highly communicative with colleagues. And if we’re not pushing our luck with asks, you ideally will possess:

Completed or pursuing a bachelor’s or higher degree in a field related to environmental building design, architecture, architectural engineering, and/ or building science
Experience with LEED certification. Other relevant sustainability certification systems are also desirable
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, AutoCAD, Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, InDesign), and Rhino
Demonstrated skills in computer and hand drafting, and sketching proficiency in written and spoken English, and good verbal, inter-personal and writing skills
In addition, skills in software such as “R,” Grasshopper, Radiance, Revit, eQuest, EnergyPlus, IES, D3, or data visualization would be desirable
Bachelor’s or higher degree in a field related to Architectural Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Architecture, Building Science, Sustainable Building Design.
1-4 years professional work experience in whole-building energy analysis, building physics, and/or high-performance HVAC design at the commercial building scale
Experience in specialized building energy simulation software (IES-VE and/or eQuest preferred, EnergyPlus and/or Grasshopper is a plus)
Ability to develop and articulate engineering problems related to HVAC system design, building envelope performance, passive conditioning strategies, building energy use, and carbon emissions.
Experience or understanding of HVAC and plumbing systems design for commercial buildings
Direct experience applying ASHRAE Standards 90.1 (particularly Appendix G modeling protocols), 55, 62.1, and 189 to new and/or existing building projects.
Experience with Green Building Rating systems (e.g., LEED, WELL, Living Building Challenge) and energy code compliance (i.e. IECC or 90.1) in various design stages.
Experience gathering and documenting energy model inputs and outputs; interpreting results and documenting the analysis in written and graphical format.
Verbal and written fluency in English
Proficiency in MS Office specifically Excel, Word and PowerPoint
Preferred credentials: BEMP, CEM, EIT, LEED GA or AP

What To Expect From Us

Competitive salary
100% paid medical, dental, and vision benefits
Generous paid time off
Emphasis on work life balance
401k matching program
Highly engaged coworkers with a shared hunger for knowledge
Mutual respect and support from colleagues and leadership
Paid Life and Disability insurance
Paid parental leave
Paid volunteer time
Pre-tax commuter benefits
Annual professional development funds
Freedom to contribute ideas and make a personal difference that is not always possible in a large corporate environment
Really good high-fives

Atelier Ten US seeks to compensate staff based on a variety of factors related to the role and the candidate. These factors include (but not limited to) the responsibilities, requirements, and location of the position, as well as the candidate/s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. We also consider internal equity, market data, and growth potential. The good faith estimate of the base compensation offered for this role is between $75,000 and $85,000. new_jobs.description:
Operations Field Manager - Restoration 
Power Dry | Columbus, OH

Who We Are
For over 37 years, Power Dry has been the trusted leader in water damage restoration, founded in the Kansas City metro area and expanding our footprint to Columbus, OH and Des Moines, IA. When water damage disrupts homes and businesses, our team delivers fast, reliable, high-quality service—bringing calm, clarity, and confidence to every situation. We build long-term partnerships by showing up, educating our clients, and doing what we say we will do.

Position Details

Job Type:
Full-time

Compensation:
Competitive base salary plus performance bonuses

Position Overview
The Operations Field Manager 
will be responsible for supervising and guiding a team of technicians in responding to property damage caused by water or mold. This role requires a proven ability to manage operations efficiently, ensure compliance with safety and quality standards, and maintain excellent customer relations. A strong knowledge of construction practices and jobsite safety protocols is essential. The ideal candidate will be proactive, detail-oriented, and highly skilled in both the technical and leadership aspects of mitigation work.

What You'll Do
Key responsibilities include:

Lead, coach, and develop the mitigation team to achieve operational excellence and exceptional customer satisfaction

Oversee mitigation projects from start to finish, ensuring quality workmanship and on-time completion

Conduct on-site inspections and provide hands-on leadership when needed

Direct crews in the field and ensure proper construction and mitigation methods are followed

Develop and improve operational workflows to maximize efficiency and productivity

Monitor project progress, resolve issues quickly, and ensure customer expectations are exceeded

Manage customer complaints and service issues through resolution, working directly with customers to address concerns and ensure a positive overall experience.

Hire, onboard, train, and mentor new team members

Conduct ongoing performance evaluations and provide coaching for continuous improvement

Collaborate with other department leaders to coordinate staffing, equipment, and project resources

Oversee inventory management and ensure equipment is properly maintained and available

Review construction plans, scopes of work, and project documentation

Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety standards, and industry best practices

Provide operational support during emergency situations, including after-hours response when needed

Monitor job costing, resource allocation, and operational performance

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience required

2–5 years of management experience in construction, restoration, or a related industry

Previous mitigation and restoration industry experience preferred

Hands-on construction experience strongly preferred

Strong understanding of financial reporting, job costing, and resource management

Demonstrated leadership experience with the ability to motivate and develop teams

Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills

Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and jobsite safety practices

Ability to read and interpret construction plans and project documentation

Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a plus

What Makes You Successful

High-energy, positive leadership style

Strong integrity and professionalism

Excellent time management and organizational skills

Customer-first mindset with the ability to remain calm under pressure

Hands-on approach and willingness to work alongside your team in the field

Ability to make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment

Benefits
We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

Competitive base salary plus performance bonuses

Bi-Weekly pay

Choice of medical plans, including select plans with $0 payroll cost for employee coverage

Dental insurance

Vision insurance

Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) for medical and dependent care expenses

Health Savings Account (HSA) available with qualifying high-deductible plans

Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance

Company-paid life insurance

401(k) with company match 

Paid time off

Paid holidays plus one floating holiday

Sick time that carries over year to year

Paid training and certification support

Opportunities for advancement and career growth

Employee referral bonus program

Company-provided uniforms

You will generate the estimate, win the client, and own the project from the first site walk to the last dollar collected. This is a seat for someone who builds business the right way, through real relationships and work that speaks for itself, not through pressure tactics.

If you would rather earn trust than push a pitch, keep reading.

What You Will Own

Bring in the work. Generate and manage technical estimates on company leads and your own referral network, meeting or exceeding the sales and profitability goals Spyder sets.
Win through credibility. Walk potential projects, scope the repair accurately, and turn one solid inspection into a client who calls you directly next time.
Be the relationship. Own the client relationship from kickoff through closeout. Keep your weekly commitments. Every interaction should be a reason they choose Spyder again.
Run the deal end to end. Prepare sharp, accurate proposals. Negotiate change orders with owners, architects, and clients. Keep budgets and financial projections honest.
Lead the room. Host project kickoffs, internal pre-construction meetings, and OAC meetings. Get the production team aligned on scope, budget, and schedule before work starts.
Step up when it gets hard. Be the escalation point project managers count on, resolve scope disputes and client issues, and help PMs grow.
The details come with the seat. You will submit RFIs and monthly pay applications, partner with accounting on down payments and receivables, build complete job folders, and attend project walks through demo, rough, punch, and final.

What You Bring

The way you are wired:
You build trust through follow-through, not flash. People do business with you because you are accurate and dependable, not because you talked them into it.
You genuinely enjoy the hunt. New relationships and new business energize you, and you are comfortable initiating them yourself.
You work independently. You do not need to be managed to deliver, and you take ownership of the outcome either way.
You care about getting it right. Precision in your estimates and your word is what keeps clients coming back.
This role is not a fit if you need a lot of oversight, prefer working from a script, or would rather manage a pipeline than build one yourself. If that is you, this probably is not your seat, and that is fine. It saves everyone time to know now.

Required:
Active Colorado Asbestos Supervisor license
Active Colorado Methamphetamine Supervisor license
7+ years estimating and managing abatement projects in Colorado
Valid Colorado driver's license and a record that meets Spyder requirements

Preferred:
Water and fire damage mitigation experience
Equipment Operator Certifications
4-year degree, preferably in Construction, Project Management, or a related field

The Work Itself

This role lives in both the office and the field. You will not be stuck at a desk.
Must be able to lift 50+ lbs, climb ladders, and work in varying weather while using full PPE as required per project.
Regular travel between job sites.
Reports to the Environmental Department Manager. No direct reports. You lead through influence and results.

Why Spyder

You will have real autonomy here. We do not micromanage people who deliver. You will work company-generated leads plus your own network, with a competitive base and performance bonuses tied to what you bring in.
Own the Outcome. Start it, finish it, own it.
Deliver Consistently. Maintain our standard, every time, everywhere.
Forge Real Relationships. Be authentic, earn trust.
Stay Gritty, Keep Growing. Push hard, keep improving.

Compensation and Benefits

Salary range: $95,000 to $140,000 annually, plus performance bonuses
Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
Company-Paid Life Insurance
401(k) with 4% Company Match
Paid Time Off and Sick Leave
Optional Accident and Critical Illness Insurance
Employee Assistance Program

What Happens Next

If your background and licenses line up, apply with your resume. After you apply, you will receive a short survey by email that takes just a few minutes. That is the only additional step before we reach out.

This posting is not a comprehensive list of duties. Responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. Spyder Construction accepts applications for this role on an ongoing basis. Spyder Construction is an equal opportunity employer.

We are committed to excellence and providing first-class service to every client on every project through clear communication, dedicated projected management, and the experience of our team.

AECOM
is seeking an Entry-Level Environmental Engineer to be based in our Rocky Hill, CT office. This position will support our Remediation team within our Environment business line.

This position is expected to begin June 2027, but that date is flexible.

Job Overview:

The Entry-Level Environmental Engineer will serve as a team member in the office and the field, assisting project and program management with site investigation, design and implementation of soil, groundwater, sediment and surface water remediation programs, data analysis, remediation construction and program management, and report preparation. This role is approximately 60% field and 40% office.

Our teams work on complex remediation projects, accessing the right resources from across the company to support project needs. By joining our team, you will have the opportunity to work on diverse projects that will challenge you technically while giving you the opportunity to work with experienced colleagues and subject matter specialists in a variety of areas. Together, these opportunities will aid in your growth in this industry.

The job responsibilities of this position may include, but are not limited to:
Project field and office support for site assessment and remediation projects.
Site visits at industrial, federal, commercial, and municipal client facilities
Data collection and analysis for environmental compliance and sustainability. Compares findings to relevant studies and local, state and federal regulations to ensure compliance.
Environmental sampling (e.g., soil, sediment, groundwater, stormwater, wastewater, air, and hazardous waste)
Development of technical memoranda and reports
Building analytic and engineering design skills under the supervision of an experienced engineer
Use of computer software (e.g. CAD, GIS, data analysis tools) as a tool for solving basic engineering problems
Performing work in accordance with agreed upon budget and schedule under supervision
Local travel is likely and U.S travel possible and project dependent.
Field work in locations as appropriate (approximately 60%).

new_jobs.description:
Are you looking for a chance to lead, innovate, and create lasting environmental impact? Join ERM
and help us build a sustainable future in Seattle, WA
.

Why This Role Matters

Are you ready to lead transformative environmental strategies for some of the most innovative technology infrastructure projects in the world? At ERM, we’re not just managing compliance—we’re shaping the future of sustainable development. This is your opportunity to join a global leader and make a measurable impact on projects that define tomorrow’s technology landscape.

What Your Impact Is

As a Managing Technical Consultant, Environmental Permitting / Due Diligence Project Manager,
you’ll be at the forefront of ERM’s Capital Project Delivery (CPD) service line, driving environmental permitting and due diligence for major capital projects. Your leadership will ensure that technology sector infrastructure developments meet environmental standards while advancing sustainability goals. You’ll influence decisions at the highest level, collaborate with global experts, and deliver solutions that balance innovation with environmental stewardship.

What You’ll Bring

Required:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering, environmental science, biology/ecology, planning, program management, or a related field. Or equivalent experience.
4+ years of relevant experience in environmental permitting and/or due diligence.
Proven ability to manage complex projects, meet deadlines, and lead multidisciplinary teams.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing technical reports and presenting to clients.
Ability to build and maintain client relationships and thrive in a fast-paced consulting environment.
This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Preferred:

Experience with permitting timelines, risk identification, and mitigation strategies.
Technical skills in wildlife or ecological surveys (e.g., wetland delineations, wildlife assessments).
Familiarity with air quality permitting and multi-media regulatory compliance programs.

Key Responsibilities

Lead environmental risk evaluations, permitting, and approvals for technology infrastructure and major capital projects.
Identify permitting requirements during site acquisition and due diligence processes.
Manage regulatory agency interactions and develop mitigation strategies for environmental risks.
Collaborate with architecture and engineering partners on conceptual master planning.
Communicate environmental requirements to diverse stakeholders, including legal, real estate, design, and sustainability teams.
Oversee preparation of reports, permitting documents, and environmental reviews at federal and state levels.
Serve as project manager, technical expert, and QA/QC reviewer to ensure quality and compliance.
Drive business development through proposal preparation and client relationship management.
Monitor project performance, budgets, schedules, and health & safety protocols.
Work across ERM’s global network to share best practices and deliver exceptional results.

For the Managing Technical Consultant, Environmental Permitting / Due Diligence Project Manager position, the anticipated annual base pay is $90,000 – $124,245 USD
. Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

: Bonuses, commissions, and other forms of additional compensation are not guaranteed and subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures.

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

new_jobs.title: Staff Environmental Engineer I
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

This position will assist the project team and Project Manager in providing field support, and technical assistance on environmental investigation and remediation projects.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in relevant technical field.
Typically requires 0-2 years of experience.
Ability to safely perform various routine field activities including but not limited to applying proper sampling techniques for all environmental media and overseeing and directing subcontractors.
Exhibits strong work ethic, positive attitude, and general enthusiasm for the work.
Entry level data evaluation and analytical skills.

Essential Duties

Field Activities:
Assists other technical staff in calibration of sampling/monitoring equipment, soil sampling, well installation, development and purging, groundwater sampling, vapor/indoor air sampling, remediation monitoring, and oversight.

Project Assistance:
Assists project team in preparation and review of data tables, soil boring logs, and figures and other components of technical reports.

Physical Demands/Work Environment Conditions

This position works predominantly in the field working independently or as part of a larger team at exterior project sites (i.e., industrial/brownfield facilities, monitoring wells, treatment systems, construction projects) to perform sample collection, recording of operational/meter parameters, and oversight of subcontractors (e.g., drillers, heavy equipment operators, truckers). These field activities require the ability to drive to different project sites and physically move around outdoors in various terrains, in adverse weather conditions and occasionally for extended or irregular hours. Conducting work involves the use of hand-held monitoring instruments and tools, as well as water sampling equipment, which requires the ability to routinely lift and carry objects, stand, walk, reach, bend, squat, kneel and twist. Office work is primarily stationary/sedentary using a computer and keyboard/mouse requiring repetitive hand movements.

Base Salary Range: $65,000 - $75,000. This salary range is based on what Roux in good faith believes it might pay at the time of posting for this position and for this geographic location. new_jobs.description:
ERM
is seeking a Technical Partner
to help grow our Natural Resources practice, with a focus on supporting power, renewable energy, diversified energy, and technology sector clients across North America.

Location: this is a hybrid role and can be based out of any of our offices across the USA

This role will provide technical leadership in biological resources, ecological mitigation, habitat conservation, ecological restoration, and environmental permitting. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to clients developing and operating major infrastructure projects while helping expand ERM's market presence and technical capabilities.

As a Partner, you will combine technical expertise, client relationship management, and business leadership to build long-term client partnerships, develop new business opportunities, and mentor multidisciplinary teams. This is an opportunity to join ERM's global partnership and play a leading role in delivering complex environmental solutions for some of North America's most significant energy and infrastructure projects.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will:

Lead business development and client engagement activities within the Power, Diversified Energy, and Technology sectors.
Provide senior technical leadership for biological resources, ecological restoration, habitat conservation, and environmental permitting programs.
Support clients through project planning, permitting, construction, and operations phases.
Develop and grow key client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.
Mentor and develop technical staff and project managers.
Collaborate with ERM partners and service line leaders to support regional and national growth initiatives.
Drive project delivery excellence while meeting financial, safety, and quality objectives.

What You'll Bring

Required:

BS/MS in environmental science, engineering, or related field.
15+ years of progressive experience in environmental consulting.
Proven leadership in mitigation and ecorestoration, including endangered species and habitat conservation.
Deep understanding of conventional and renewable energy markets in North America.
Strong business development track record, generating and delivering multi-million-dollar programs.
Expertise in HCPs, and regional permitting.

Preferred:

Experience establishing mitigation banks and writing vegetation management plans.
Existing client relationships in the Power, Diversified energy and/or Technology sector that can be leveraged for growth.
Familiarity with utility commissions, regulatory agencies, and emerging sustainability trends.

Why ERM?

Equity Ownership: Be a shareholder in a purpose-driven, global firm.
Strategic Influence: Shape the direction of ERM and the future of sustainable infrastructure.
Thought Leadership: Lead conversations that matter in energy, ecology, and sustainability.
Global Reach, Local Impact: Leverage ERM’s platform to amplify your influence and deliver measurable results.

Application
s accepted through September 30, 2026

new_jobs.title: Director/Senior Attorney, Land Conservation
new_jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Land Conservation Director/Senior Attorney will lead a team of experienced land conservation advocates who focus on safeguarding our priceless public lands to preserve critical ecological and cultural values. This includes working defensively against the onslaught of attempts to sell off public lands, protecting bedrock conservation laws, elevating targeted campaigns in priority landscapes, and promoting durable, conservation focused solutions to meeting energy demands. The Director will play an important leadership role in NRDC’s lands work - joining the Lands Division Leadership team, collaborating with teams and leadership across NRDC, and engaging on external campaigns and coalitions. In addition to serving as a Senior Attorney and thought leader for Land Conservation advocacy, the Director will oversee the team’s day-to-day work, engage in fundraising, guide communications efforts, and help lead priority state and federal legislative and administrative advocacy campaigns.

This role will operate in a hybrid remote capacity in any of our US NRDC Offices (
Chicago, Santa Monica, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C.)

Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions:
Manage the land conservation team, which consists of lawyers, scientists and policy advocates advancing critical land conservation efforts, including public lands defense and conservation focused solutions to meeting energy demands.
Develop and lead Land Conservation team strategies and goals, ensuring alignment with fundraising, institutional priorities, team members expertise and capacity, and key partnerships.
Represent NRDC and the Land Conservation team as an authoritative source both internally as well as externally in public forums, including administrative proceedings, legislative committee hearings, and media outlets.
Build and maintain relationships with partners, coalitions, decisionmakers, and other stakeholders to guide strategy, influence policy outcomes, and identify advocacy needs.
Oversee staff performance and provide mentoring, guidance, and on-going feedback to ensure that staff develop and reach performance goals that support division priorities, institutional DEI, professional development, and management needs.
Provide legal expertise and guidance to Nature Leadership and staff, including other NRDC departments, on priority strategies and related legal, technical and/or policy issues; and help develop and oversee litigation on priority public lands issues, in collaboration with NRDC’s Litigation Team.

The above list of duties is not comprehensive but generally demonstrates the types of matters under this position’s responsibility. Other duties may be assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Education & Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience required, with authoritative knowledge concerning land conservation. Law degree required.; litigation experience preferred.
7+ years of experience of legal and/or policy advocacy, including 3 years of management experience. Experience leading state or federal campaigns, litigating and advocating for public lands preferred.
Experience successfully building and navigating diverse teams and/or coalitions, including developing consensus on policy issues and driving toward equitable, positive outcomes.

Skills, Abilities, Competencies

An ability to foster and cultivate a positive, inclusive and equitable working environment with colleagues, leadership and external stakeholders.
Advanced interpersonal skills and the ability to provide leadership, guidance, feedback, and coaching in the context of employee engagement, team/coalition building, and project and people management.
Excellent organizational and project management skills.
An ability to effectively communicate and deploy written and verbal skills to advance complex concepts.
Excellent strategic judgment, integrity, professional discretion, and ability to handle sensitive/confidential matters.
Ability to travel to NRDC U.S. based offices, approximately 20% annually
Commitment to NRDC’s mission, values, and DEI principles

-------------------------------------
NRDC (the Natural Resources Defense Council) works to safeguard the Earth, its people, its plants and animals, and the natural systems on which all life depends. NRDC combines the power of more than 3 million members and online activists with the expertise of some 800 policy advocates, lawyers, scientists, and communication experts to confront the climate crisis, protect nature, ensure the rights of all people to clean air, clean water, and healthy communities. As an international nonprofit environmental organization, NRDC is working to address the world’s most urgent environmental challenges, and advance innovative, science-based, and enforceable solutions.

Since our founding in 1970, NRDC has helped craft and deliver many of America’s foundational environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act. Today, we continue to lead in advancing and defending strong environmental protections at the local, state, federal and international levels, as well as through the marketplace. Our team works across the United States and around the world, from offices in Chicago, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., as well as in Beijing, and New Delhi (a subsidiary of NRDC India Pvt. Ltd.).

Supported by our members and online activists, NRDC is driving impactful solutions that confront the climate crisis, defend nature and safeguard public health across Asia, Africa, and the Americas. At NRDC, we believe lasting change happens when people bring their talent, passion, and expertise together for a common purpose: to build a cleaner, healthier, and more resilient world. Learn more at nrdc.org
-----------------------------
PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position within the described work environment.
Frequently
: Perform desk-based computer tasks
Frequently
: Ability to interact and communicate with employees and others as necessary
Frequently
: Attend planned meetings and collaborate with management and coworkers
Frequently:
Hand draw illustrations for advocacy materials
Occasionally
: Ability to attend events and activities in the office or offsite
Work is sometimes performed primarily in office. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in office settings and moderate in other situations. Hours of employment may sometimes require working flexible and/or longer hours, including nights and weekends, when necessitated by projects. The job includes work-related situations such as those involving challenging, important, urgent, time-sensitive, or multiple matters.

NRDC is committed to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion, both in our work and in our workplace. We believe that celebrating and actively welcoming diverse voices and perspectives is essential to solving the planet's most pressing environmental problems, and we encourage applications from candidates whose identities have been historically under-represented in the environmental movement.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits , and a supportive working environment. Salary is based on a nonprofit scale and is commensurate with skills and experience. Internal equity will be reviewed and considered to determine a final offer. For this position, the salary range is $162,000 to $180,000.

Perks & Benefits

Not only do we care about taking care of our planet, we care about taking care of you. When you join our team, we invest in your total well-being. Here is a small glimpse on how we plan to support you:

Time to Unplug & Recharge:
Enjoy a generous time-off policy, highlighted by a company-wide year-end Rest & Recharge Week to reset for the new year.

For your Future
: Matching 403b whether you contribute or not
Hybrid Policy:
The freedom to balance your time around your needs that means, 8 days per month in-office. In-office day requirements can be met with off-site work events such as retreats, conferences, and other work-related travel.
Well – being
: Premium Comprehensive healthcare and mental health programs.

Due to the high volume of applications, we will contact only those candidates we would like to interview. Please no phone calls, emails, or in-person résumé drop-offs.

If you experience technical problems while applying or if you are a person with a disability and need assistance applying online, please reach out to iCIMS Customer Care at 1-800-889-4422.

new_jobs.title: Geospatial Surveyor
new_jobs.description:
Join a team delivering complex, high-impact projects that shape infrastructure, utilities and the built environment across the UK. At Tetra Tech, you’ll combine advanced geospatial expertise with real project ownership, working on technically challenging surveys that support major programmes across water, defence, nuclear and infrastructure sectors.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Geospatial Surveyor, you will deliver surveying and geospatial projects from initial planning through to final delivery, supporting a diverse range of technically demanding projects across the UK. Working within a collaborative national team, you’ll combine field-based surveying with office-based data processing and analysis to produce high-quality outputs for clients across multiple sectors.

This role offers genuine variety, autonomy and client exposure, giving you the opportunity to take ownership of projects while developing your technical and professional capabilities in a supportive environment focused on innovation, collaboration and continuous development.

Your Impact in this Position

You’ll play a key role in delivering accurate geospatial information that supports critical engineering, infrastructure and asset management decisions. Your expertise in surveying, data capture and interpretation will help clients manage complex projects safely, efficiently and effectively.

By building strong client relationships and delivering reliable technical outputs, you’ll contribute directly to successful project outcomes while strengthening the reputation of Tetra Tech’s Geospatial team across the UK and beyond.

Core Capabilities
Geospatial Survey Delivery

Deliver geospatial surveying projects from inception through to completion
Carry out topographical, setting-out, measured building, levelling and laser scanning surveys

Data Capture & Technical Analysis

Capture, process and interpret high-quality survey data using industry-leading technologies
Produce accurate outputs using AutoCAD, Leica Infinity and related software tools

Survey Technology Expertise

Operate Total Station and GNSS equipment confidently across varied project environments
Apply modern surveying techniques to support technically complex projects

Client & Project Collaboration

Build strong working relationships with clients and multidisciplinary project teams
Balance site-based and office-based responsibilities while managing competing priorities effectively

Professionalism & Adaptability

Work independently with a proactive, solutions-focused approach
Adapt to different sectors, project locations and operational requirements

Training, Qualifications & Experience

Experience in topographical surveying, survey software and GNSS/Total Station equipment is essential, alongside strong communication and client-facing skills. Experience with laser scanning, levelling, measured building surveys or terrain modelling would be advantageous, as would a relevant technical qualification. A full UK driving licence is required.

Working Environment

This role offers a balance of site, office and hybrid working, with flexibility available where practical to support work/life balance. Projects are located across the UK, with occasional international opportunities and travel depending on project requirements. You’ll join a collaborative and supportive team environment with opportunities for professional development and chartership support.

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. We have a wide range of expertise across our teams, providing a global support network with a personalised approach to client relationships to better understand where we can add value. We provide a collaborative environment that supports individual performance, innovation, and creativity.

We support public and private sector clients on local, national, and international projects to deliver sustainable and resilient solutions. Our operations in the UK, Ireland, and the Netherlands include more than 6,000 employees who are Leading with Science® to solve our clients’ most complex problems.

In alignment with the Equality Act 2010, we will make reasonable adjustments to support candidates and employees requiring additional arrangements. This could include adaptations to work schedules, training approaches, or the physical workspace. Role Title: Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant

Start Date: September 2027

Location: Leeds, Manchester or Edinburgh

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Launch your career on projects that help transform brownfield land, protect communities and support a more sustainable future. At Tetra Tech, you’ll work alongside experienced specialists, develop practical consultancy skills and contribute to projects that form part of our ambition to improve the lives of 1 billion people.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant, you will join our Geo team, delivering geo-environmental consultancy services supported by in-house ground investigation expertise. You will work across contaminated land, site investigation, brownfield redevelopment and geotechnical engineering projects for clients in sectors including property and regeneration, defence estates and transport.

Your Impact in this position

You will support the design, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental ground investigations. Your work will include desk studies, accurate collection and interpretation of site data, ground gas and groundwater monitoring, assessment of findings and production of detailed technical reports. This is an excellent opportunity to gain varied project experience and build a long-term career within a growing team.

5 Core Capabilities

Ground investigation: Support the planning, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental investigations across a range of sites and sectors.
Geo-environmental assessment: Undertake desk-based studies and develop your understanding of contaminated land, brownfield redevelopment, site investigation and geotechnical engineering.
Site data and monitoring: Collect, analyse and interpret site information accurately, including ground gas and groundwater monitoring data.
Technical reporting: Produce clear, detailed and well-structured reports that communicate findings and support sound project decisions.
Professional development and collaboration: Work effectively both independently and as part of a team, use initiative, build strong communication skills and work towards professional qualification with support from mentors and colleagues.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

You will have, or expect to achieve, at least a 2:1 degree in geology, engineering geology, environmental science or a related subject. Enthusiasm, analytical ability, strong written, communication and presentation skills, and a commitment to professional development are essential. Relevant work experience, such as a placement, is desirable. A full driving licence is required. Some projects may require security clearance, so you must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate clearance.

Working Environment

Based in either Leeds, Manchester or Edinburgh you will work across office, project and site environments, with travel required to client and investigation sites. Hybrid working is available; however, as this is a graduate role, you will be expected to spend more time in the office initially to support training, mentoring and your transition into the team. As your knowledge, confidence and competence develop, greater flexibility may be available in line with project and team requirements.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

Tetra Tech Europe is an industry-leading multi-national, multi-disciplinary consultancy. Our Environmental Planning Team supports the continued growth of the UK Environment, Sustainability & Planning (ESP) team and wider business, delivering environmental co-ordination, EIA and related assessment and management work across renewables/energy, water/utilities, residential, defence, infrastructure, waste and minerals. You’ll join a team with an established workload, a strong reputation, ISEP EIA Quality Mark membership and active involvement in industry working groups, presentations and conferences.

Your Impact in this position

Working with support from senior colleagues, you’ll contribute to environmental planning, optioneering and impact assessment across a varied project portfolio. You’ll help deliver work to programme, budget and quality standards, build your skills in project management, business development and technical assessment, and produce technically robust outputs that inform responsible project decisions.

Project Co-ordination Support – Support project managers across multiple projects, working with teams, stakeholders and subcontractors, and helping programme site surveys.

Report Writing and Communication – Prepare clear reports such as EIAs and CEMPs, present findings where needed, and review deliverables for accuracy and compliance.
Collaboration Across Disciplines – Work with colleagues in air quality, biodiversity, land use, transport and other teams to assess impacts and mitigation.

A Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Management or a related field, plus academic and/or practical EIA experience. Knowledge of environmental laws, regulations, guidelines and the UK planning/consenting process is essential, alongside strong communication, coordination, time management, problem-solving, attention to detail and analytical skills.

Role Title: Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant

Start Date: September 2027

Location: Leeds, Manchester or Edinburgh

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Launch your career on projects that help transform brownfield land, protect communities and support a more sustainable future. At Tetra Tech, you’ll work alongside experienced specialists, develop practical consultancy skills and contribute to projects that form part of our ambition to improve the lives of 1 billion people.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant, you will join our Geo team, delivering geo-environmental consultancy services supported by in-house ground investigation expertise. You will work across contaminated land, site investigation, brownfield redevelopment and geotechnical engineering projects for clients in sectors including property and regeneration, defence estates and transport.

Your Impact in this position

You will support the design, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental ground investigations. Your work will include desk studies, accurate collection and interpretation of site data, ground gas and groundwater monitoring, assessment of findings and production of detailed technical reports. This is an excellent opportunity to gain varied project experience and build a long-term career within a growing team.

5 Core Capabilities

Ground investigation: Support the planning, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental investigations across a range of sites and sectors.
Geo-environmental assessment: Undertake desk-based studies and develop your understanding of contaminated land, brownfield redevelopment, site investigation and geotechnical engineering.
Site data and monitoring: Collect, analyse and interpret site information accurately, including ground gas and groundwater monitoring data.
Technical reporting: Produce clear, detailed and well-structured reports that communicate findings and support sound project decisions.
Professional development and collaboration: Work effectively both independently and as part of a team, use initiative, build strong communication skills and work towards professional qualification with support from mentors and colleagues.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

You will have, or expect to achieve, at least a 2:1 degree in geology, engineering geology, environmental science or a related subject. Enthusiasm, analytical ability, strong written, communication and presentation skills, and a commitment to professional development are essential. Relevant work experience, such as a placement, is desirable. A full driving licence is required. Some projects may require security clearance, so you must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate clearance.

Working Environment

Based in either Leeds, Manchester or Edinburgh you will work across office, project and site environments, with travel required to client and investigation sites. Hybrid working is available; however, as this is a graduate role, you will be expected to spend more time in the office initially to support training, mentoring and your transition into the team. As your knowledge, confidence and competence develop, greater flexibility may be available in line with project and team requirements.
